sections.h2: Who to call about a Woodford County tax matter
sections.html:
Questions about what a property is worth go to the Property Valuation Administrator. Questions about what you owe go to the sheriff. The valuation office is in the courthouse at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, Versailles, and it opens at 8 each morning, closing at 4 Monday to Thursday and 5:30 on Friday. For the sheriff, call 859-873-3119 or 859-873-3126; the website has bill search with online payment.

A notice stating each property's value reaches owners in spring. The sheriff sends bills out during the final week of September, with overdue notices going out in February. The sheriff never mails threatening demands for property tax, so a letter from an unfamiliar "unit" with an 800 number should be reported, and the demand ignored.

sections.h2: What a seller of a Woodford County house should know
sections.html:
Woodford sits in the Bluegrass inside the Lexington metro area. Versailles is the seat and the biggest town; Midway is the only other city. The county had 27,883 residents in 2025, a 3.8 percent gain over 2020, and 11,917 housing units. Builders pulled 95 permits in 2025.

  • The middle owned home is worth $299,700.
  • A typical household earns $83,788, and 71.7 percent of households are owners.
  • Rent runs $1,138. Owners pay $1,571 with a mortgage and $577 without.

With prices like these, even a modest assessment gap shows up in the bill, so the steps below are worth the effort. Before you list, find out whether the PVA's value looks close to what comparable houses have sold for, and whether any exemption is on your parcel. A buyer's agent will look at the tax bill when estimating monthly costs, and a figure that is out of line can make a house harder to sell. If the roll is not open yet, plan around the first Monday in May, when the display begins.

If you want to ask about a value or an exemption in person, the courthouse counter in Room 108 is the place. Bring your parcel number or address, and write down the name of whoever helps you and the date.

sections.h2: Your tax year in Woodford County
sections.html:
The calendar is statewide and set out in KRS 134.015.

Yearly property tax steps for a Woodford County owner
WhenStep
January 1Assessment date; whoever is the owner of record that day is the taxpayer
Opening Monday of May, 13 daysRoll on public display
25 to 35 days laterLocal appeals board sits
Up to November 1Discount of 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount of the bill
JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February onwardAdd 10 percent
April 15Unpaid bills go from the sheriff to the clerk, which records a lien

If you list in spring, last year's bill is still yours when your name was on the January 1 roll. Get a balance in writing from the sheriff for your title company.

sections.h2: How does a Woodford County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
First, sit down with the PVA office. The state demands that conference, and the office has to walk you through how it reached your number and write down what each side claims. After that, the appeal goes to the County Clerk, and it must arrive by closing time the next workday once the display ends.

  • Bring evidence: details of the building and lot, insurance records, construction costs, and sales listings. Without evidence the appeal is denied.
  • Anyone you pay to represent you must be a recognized professional, such as an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and needs your written permission.
  • You may record the hearing, and the board has to put any change in writing.

If you skip the local board, the Kentucky Claims Commission is closed to you. If bills print before your case ends and the final value comes out above your claim, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

The method depends on the property. Houses are compared to nearby sales, with adjustments for things like a basement. Barns and other farm structures are priced as replacement cost minus depreciation, and income property is valued from its earnings. Farmland is assessed on its agricultural worth under Section 172A of the state constitution, which can sharply lower the tax on open pasture. Anyone planning to divide a farm should ask both the PVA and the clerk what changes when the use changes.

Any parcel can be revalued yearly, and each must be inspected at least every fourth year. If your figure looks too high, ask the PVA which sales it relied on and when staff last inspected the house.

A homeowner who turns 65, or who is totally disabled, gets a fixed amount deducted from the assessed value of their residence, one deduction per household. The claim goes on Form 62A350 at the PVA office. The exemption carries on while the same applicant stays. An owner with a service connected disability rating, or anyone with a permanent Social Security disability finding, files once. A buyer applies fresh, and the PVA can quote the current sum, which the state revisits every two years.

After a sale, notify the PVA so your old address loses the deduction and the next owner can start a claim.

Right after the clerk records the lien, interest begins at 1 percent a month. Next comes a 10 percent clerk commission, then a 20 percent attorney commission. The attorney sends two notices, one at 30 days and one later, before a sale, which falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer. KRS 134.420 lets the lien run for 11 years, and it stays with the parcel. If you sell, it comes out of your proceeds. A private buyer who purchases the certificate may add fees.

sections.h2: Selling with a bill still open
sections.html:
Call the sheriff about the current year and the clerk about anything that crossed over on April 15. Ask for both numbers in writing, since the title company subtracts them from your payout. When a private buyer already holds a certificate, you pay that buyer, fees included, so find out who holds it.

Some cash buyers take the house with the bill still open and settle the balance from the proceeds, so you do not have to pay ahead of a sale you are still arranging. In any sale, the contract should name who covers the current year, because the January 1 owner is the one named on the bill. A written split also prevents a dispute after the keys change hands.

faqs.q: Who sends out Woodford County tax bills each year?
faqs.a: The sheriff mails them during the last week of September. Call 859-873-3119 or 859-873-3126, or use the website for bill search plus online payment.

faqs.q: How can a Woodford County owner push back on a valuation?
faqs.a: Schedule the PVA conference, then lodge the appeal with the County Clerk the next workday after public display ends. The PVA is at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles.

faqs.q: When does the 2 percent Woodford County discount stop?
faqs.a: It ends November 1. The printed amount is due until December 31, then 5 percent is added for January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: If a Woodford County house sells in spring, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is taxed and appears on the bill. The sale contract and title company decide who pays at closing, so get a written sheriff balance first.

faqs.q: What are good questions for the Woodford County PVA?
faqs.a: Ask which recent sales back your value and when staff last inspected the house. The answers tell you if an appeal is worth the effort before May.
